$comment: THE BRIEF: the rubric and the evidence brief.html grades a job ad with.
A recruiter pastes a job ad; the page maps each requirement to the work on this site
that backs it, lists the gaps as plainly as the matches, lists what only Moses can
confirm, and selects the case studies that match into a dossier to print or forward. It is
deterministic matching in the browser over this file and content/profile.json: no AI,
and the ad never leaves the page. These were the Assay's rules (modules/interactives.js),
moved here unchanged in what they match and say, so the validator can hold them to the
- every evidence link goes to a case study, a public artifact, a research output or a
part of the homepage that exists, written as the page it is on (index.html#experience);
- a strength's caseStudies exist, and include every case study its evidence links to;
- every figure an evidence line or a gap prints is one content/claims.json holds;
- every id is kebab-case and unique across the file, and every pattern compiles.
npm run build:content writes what the page needs of this file into brief.html, beside
the facts it may state (from content/profile.json only: the roles, the degrees and
`languages`) and, for each named tool, where the homepage shows it.
The ids are what a shared link carries (brief.html?focus=...): the grade, the strengths
matched, and each named requirement met, missed or to confirm. A tool's id and a
language's are its name in lower case, spaces as hyphens ("power-bi"). Never the ad.
$minWords: Fewer words than this, and there is nothing to grade honestly.
$grades: What each grade is called. The top grade needs no hard gap and broad coverage of the ad;
a hard gap caps it (why: docs/plan.md, Phase 0 step 7). `domain` counts areas of this
site's own field, not marked general below: an HR or ERP ad used to grade High on
general ones alone, and with no domain area at all the grade is "Different field".
$requirementCues: A line with one of these asks for something even if nothing below recognises it, and an unanswered one counts against coverage: the thing that stops three matches in a long ad reading as a fit. Stems: "manag" finds "management".
$softCues: An unmet requirement on a line like this is listed but does not cap the grade: the ad itself says it can do without it.
$softHeading: Whole-line headings only: "Required: SAP" is a requirement.
hardHeading: ^(requirements?|required|must[- ]haves?|qualifications|what you bring|who you are|you have|your profile|profile|responsibilities|what you('ll| will) do)\s*:?$
$strengths: Capability areas backed by delivered work, each with the evidence and where on the site it is.
A `general` one counts, never alone. Synonyms match whole words in any case, with an optional
plural. `caseStudies` are the case studies the dossier selects when the area matches, the one
its evidence is nearest first; the dossier ranks them by how many matched areas name them.

$tools: Named methods, tools and platforms: matched only where the homepage shows the tool, a gap
anywhere else. A bare name matches itself in any case. A `re` is a regular expression, alone
or beside synonyms, for the names only case or punctuation tells apart from ordinary words:
"SAP", "R" (not "R&D"), "Excel", "LCA". Where the homepage shows each is read from it by the
build, best proof first: the skills toolkit (it carries a proof line), then the experience
bullets, the project tags, the courses and the skill lists. A tool the homepage stops
$languages: content/profile.json records no languages today, so each one an ad asks for is a gap until
it does. English, the site's own, is not a gap, but its level is not stated either: until it
is, it is one to confirm, and a line asking only for it is not graded.
$languageCues: "Dutch" on a line about a ministry is a nationality. On a line with one of these, or of four words or fewer, it is a language; a clause over four words needs its own ("...German partners, in fluent English" asks for English alone). A clause of languages only runs on past its comma: "German, French or Spanish at C1".
$applyIn: The language to write an application in is not one the job needs: "Applications in English or Dutch are welcome".
$nationalStems: Never a language when the next word starts with one of these, or is a name ("Dutch Tax Authority"): that is the employer, not the job.
$levels: Highest first: the first that matches a line is the level it asks for. CEFR codes match in capitals only. No level stated means defaultLevel, B2.
$years: "5+ years", "minimum of 7 years", "at least three years", "3-5 years" (the lower bound).
"5+" or "at least 5" is a requirement anywhere; a bare "3 years", or "over 20 years", only
beside an experience cue or under a requirements heading. Never on a line about the contract
or the calendar, nor where the employer talks about itself ("For over 20 years, we have..."),
not to the applicant. Years are counted from content/profile.json, professional roles only:
a title with one of notCountedAsYears is training or a placement.
$gaps: Hard requirements the site cannot show, beyond tools, languages and years. `cue` must also be
on the line, so "As one of the Big Four, we..." is not a demand; `not` rules a line out;
